facts.F1: Story #6361 S03c Package Forecasting, nwdes feature C of three (cycle and rules). First, a public examine command shows forecasts being recomputed after a Team refresh and the start-up forecast seeding firing, on demo data, so the examiner can observe the moved triggers, updater and seeder working. Then break the Flow metrics to Forecasting cycle by inverting Flow metrics' three edges through ports Flow metrics owns (IThroughputFilter, IForecastDataSufficiency, IHowManyForecaster), answered by Forecasting; Forecasting keeps depending on Flow metrics. Give Forecasting its own module rules (types in their layer, Domain reaches only the kernel, outside reaches Domain, Adapters and Application only from the lists, Application outbound) with inline lists, take the Forecasting entries off Flow metrics' inbound list and empty its Forecasting outbound list, and make the shared rule wording a parameter. Move Forecasting's unit tests to Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Modules/Forecasting with a placement test. Behaviour-free: routes, DTOs, responses, metrics answers, forecast results, handler order, DI lifetimes and the schema stay the same. Design: docs/feature/story-6361-s03c-package-forecasting/feature-delta.md (slices C1-C3, D-3, D-6, D-9, Ratchet design R-F1..R-F6, Notes from the feature B reviews).

facts.F2: Forecasting is a module of its own with its own rules, and Flow metrics no longer depends on it, so the Flow metrics and Forecasting cycle is gone and Epic 6474 slice 07 can write into Forecasting's seam

facts.F6: Forecasting's unit tests live under Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Modules/Forecasting and a placement test keeps them there
facts.F7: Metrics answers, forecasts and forecast answers are identical before and after the change, and forecasts still refresh after a Team refresh and at start-up
